data.name: Bahirun
data.gender_notes: Bahirun is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who has a bright and clear vision, a seer. The name Bahirun carries the meaning “Shining, Bright, Clear” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Bahirun usually hope their child will grow to embody shining, bright, clear and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Bahirun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Shining, Bright, Clear.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bahirun total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_english.name: Bahirun
in_english.long_meaning: Bahirun is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, derived from 'bahir', meaning shining, radiant, or bright. The name signifies light, clarity, and manifestation. In the Quran, it appears in contexts emphasizing appearance and clarity. Bahirun holds spiritual significance in Islamic tradition, symbolizing illumination and enlightenment. It is chosen for its positive connotations and deep etymological roots in Arabic linguistics

data.cultural_impact: The name "Bahirun" carries a rich cultural significance in the Islamic world. It is rooted in the Arabic language, which has greatly influenced Islamic thought and culture. The term "Bahir" means "outside" or "exterior" in Arabic, while "un" means "light" or "bright." Thus, "Bahirun" can be translated as "one who has a bright and clear vision," or "a seer." This name has been used by scholars and spiritual leaders in Islamic history, symbolizing a deep understanding of the world around us and the ability to see beyond the surface.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Bahirun" holds a deep spiritual significance in Islamic thought. It reflects the idea that true vision and understanding come from a connection to the divine. The name signifies the importance of spiritual purification and the development of inner wisdom and insight.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Shining, Bright, Clear" symbolizes One who has a bright and clear vision, a seer. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Bahirun serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of shining, bright, clear.

historical_references.reference: Al-Biruni, Muhammad ibn Ahmad (973-1048 CE). He was a Persian polymath who wrote over a hundred works covering various fields of knowledge: astronomy, mathematics, geography, philosophy, theology, and history. Al-Biruni is considered one of the greatest scholars of the Islamic Golden Age. In his work 'Al-Athar al-Baqiyah fi Tarikh al-Hind' (On the Remaining Signs of India), he described Indian mathematics and provided the earliest known detailed description of the Indians' decimal positional notation system. The work also contained one of the earliest known descriptions of Indian society and culture. He is sometimes referred to as 'Bahirun' or 'Bahar-i A'zam' in India, which translates to 'the greatest among those who shed light', in acknowledgement of his contribution to the understanding of the Indian subcontinent.

Al-Biruni, Muhammad ibn Ahmad. He was born in Khwarezm (present-day Uzbekistan) and studied in Kath (Bukhara) and Gurgan. He traveled extensively throughout the Islamic world, including to India, where he stayed for several years. He is best known for his work 'Kitab al-Tabqiq fi Ma'rifat al-Hind' (The Reality of India), which contains a detailed description of the geography, people, and culture of India. Al-Biruni was a pioneer in the field of Indology and his work greatly influenced European knowledge of India until the arrival of European travelers in the 18th century. He is also known for his works on mathematics, astronomy, and philosophy. The name 'Bahirun' is a Persian title meaning 'the illuminated one' or 'the enlightened one', which reflects his contributions to various fields of knowledge.
